title: Stage 2: Services and the database
summary: Give the API a stable address and run PostgreSQL with its own disk.

steps.title: Two Services and a StatefulSet
body: ports: [{ port: 80, targetPort: http }]      # 'http' is the named containerPort 8080
clusterIP: None                               # headless: db-0.db.shop resolves to the pod
env: [{ name: PGDATA, value: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata }]   # a subfolder: a fresh disk has lost+found at its root
The API reaches the database at `db-0.db.shop.svc.cluster.local:5432` (or simply `db:5432` from inside `shop`).

steps.prompt: What is the PVC created for `db-0` called?
steps.explain: `<template name>-<statefulset name>-<ordinal>`. It survives the pod and is reattached when `db-0` is recreated.

steps.prompt: The API pods are labelled `app: shop-api` and listen on the named port `http` (8080). Complete the Service.
steps.explain: The API stays internal; stage 5's Gateway route (HTTPRoute) is the only way in from outside.

items: other pods call the API at a stable name
traffic only goes to ready API pods
`db-0.db.shop` resolves to the database pod's IP
the database keeps its disk when the pod moves
the database pod is always called `db-0`

steps.title: Give the API and the database stable names
prompt: This terminal runs a **real one-node Kubernetes 1.37 cluster** (k3s) with `kubectl`; the current namespace is `todo`, and the manifests live in `~/k8s`. `todo-api` (port named `http`) and the database StatefulSet `todo-db` (PostgreSQL stand-in,
port named `postgres` on 5432) run, but nothing can reach them by name. Write `~/k8s/services.yaml` with two Services
1. `todo-api` on port 80, to the API pods' `http` port;
2. `todo-db` on port 5432, to the database pod's `postgres` port.
From the `shell` pod: `kubectl exec shell -- wget -qO- -T 2 http://todo-api/` and
`kubectl exec shell -- nc -w 2 todo-db 5432` both answer.

checks.name: todo-api answers by name
checks.cmd: timeout 20 sh -c 'until kubectl exec shell -- wget -qO- -T 3 http://todo-api/ 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^Name:"; do sleep 1; done' ; kubectl exec shell -- wget -qO- -T 3 http://todo-api/ | grep '^Name:'

checks.name: both target named ports
checks.cmd: kubectl get svc todo-api todo-db -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}={.spec.ports[0].port}->{.spec.ports[0].targetPort} {end}'
checks.fail: Use the named container ports as `targetPort` (`http`, `postgres`).

hints: A Service: `selector` (the pods' labels) and `ports: [{port: ..., targetPort: ...}]`.
`targetPort` may name a container port: `targetPort: http`.
Two documents in one file separated by `---`, then `kubectl apply -f ~/k8s/services.yaml`.
steps.explain: Services give pods a stable name and virtual IP while the pods behind them come and go. Named `targetPort`s keep the Service right when a container's port number changes. For a real PostgreSQL StatefulSet you would usually add a headless Service (`clusterIP: None`) for stable per-pod names, plus this regular one for clients.
